boundary_rationale: Opens the book with a sequential-temporal formula ('After the death of Joshua') tying it to the just-closed Joshua account, then an inquiry formula ('asked of Yahweh, saying, Who should go up') answered by a divine oracle ('Judah shall go up. Behold, I have delivered the land into his hand'). v3 pivots to human implementation as Judah addresses Simeon directly, a change of interlocutor and speech-act that closes this unit before the campaign narrative begins. This same inquiry-and-oracle pair recurs near-verbatim at Judg.20.18 (מִי יַעֲלֶה לָּנוּ בַתְּחִלָּה / וַיֹּאמֶר יְהוָה יְהוּדָה בַתְּחִלָּה), an inclusio bracketing the whole book; disclosed as corroboration for this unit's coherence, though it does not resolve the opening edge, which has nothing preceding it within Judges.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading v3 as the oracle's direct enactment might argue for pulling it into this unit - but that verse swaps Yahweh for Simeon as addressee and trades the inquiry-oracle genre for an alliance proposal, a clean enough formula reset to end the unit at v2 instead.

boundary_rationale: Opens with Judah's direct proposal to Simeon ('Come up with me into my lot'), replacing the inquiry-oracle exchange, and runs through the Adoni-Bezek capture and its talionic saying without a new speech-formula break into the Jerusalem conquest (v8), since v7's closing wayyiqtol chain ('brought him to Jerusalem, and he died there') carries no subject reset into v8's own action ('The children of Judah fought against Jerusalem'). A pe falls after 1:7 in both Masoretic witnesses (parashah_two_witness), exactly at the seam the rejected alternative proposes; disclosed here as weak, Prophets-tier corroboration for that alternative, not treated as a driver. Closes at v8's capture-and-burn notice; v9 opens a fresh geographic transition formula naming three new regions.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting v3-7 (Adoni-Bezek, closed by 'he died there') from v8 (Jerusalem) was considered, corroborated weakly by the pe after 1:7; rejected because v8's clause continues without any subject reset from v7's closing chain, the grammatical continuity outweighing the toponym alone. (The earlier ground for rejection - that v7 'names Jerusalem as the destination' - conflated Adoni-Bezek's place of death with the object of Judah's separate campaign and is withdrawn as the stated reason.)

boundary_rationale: Opens with the temporal-geographic transition 'After that, the children of Judah went down to fight...' naming three regions (hill country/South/lowland), distinct from the preceding Jerusalem-focused notice. Itemizes Hebron and Debir (each with a name-note) and the marriage-prize proposal for whoever takes Kiriath Sepher, fulfilled by Othniel. Closes at v13's fulfillment ('gave him Achsah his daughter as his wife'); v14 pivots to a new participant-focus as Achsah herself becomes the acting subject, marking the edge.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Keeping the whole Achsah episode together through v15 has surface appeal, yet v14 makes her the acting, initiating subject in place of the male-conquest-and-reward pattern governing 9-13 - enough of a participant shift to stand as its own beat.

boundary_rationale: Opens with Achsah as the initiating subject ('she got him to ask her father for a field') and closes with her direct-speech request and its grant ('give me also springs of water. Then Caleb gave her the upper springs and the lower springs')-a self-contained request-and-grant beat. v16 shifts subject entirely to the Kenites, a new clan notice with no link to Caleb's household.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating vv14-15 as a mere coda to 9-13 rather than an independent unit was considered; rejected because the type-scene closes on its own completed transaction (request voiced, request granted), a shape shared with the parallel doublet at Josh.15.18-19.

boundary_rationale: Opens with a fresh subject reset ('The children of the Kenite...went up') and gathers loosely related notices - Kenite settlement, the Hormah etiology, Philistine coastal cities taken (including v19's 'could not drive out' notice for the valley inhabitants), an evaluative summary about iron chariots, and a resumptive Hebron/Caleb notice echoing v10. The prior claim that no internal seam carries a distinct marker is false: 1:17 opens with an explicit subject reset (Judah with Simeon, resuming 1:3) after 1:16's Kenite notice. The span is nonetheless kept whole on content-uniformity grounds: vv16-20 read as one loosely-associated settlement/itinerary register sharing the same immediate geographic and tribal frame as vv9-15's Judah campaign, with no independent scene, dialogue, or completed transaction of the kind that closes other spans in this cluster. This differs from the disjunctive Kenite-adjacent clause at 4:11 (M8-Judg-026), isolated there as its own decision: 4:11's aside has no narrative connection to what follows for three chapters (a genuine proleptic authorial parenthesis), while 1:16's notice is an immediate component of the same itinerary the surrounding verses narrate. The disjunctive clause-form is the same at both sites; the narrative function differs, which is the stated reason for the different treatment. Also disclosed: the 'could not drive out' formula family appears in three configurations across this stretch of the book - absorbed as one clause among many at 1:19 (here), isolated as an entire, etiologically-closed verse at 1:21 (M8-Judg-006), and gathered into a uniform six-entry register at 1:27-36 (M8-Judg-008) - three structurally distinct, principled outcomes rather than one inconsistently applied rule.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting at 1:16/1:17, since 1:17 does carry an explicit subject reset (Judah with Simeon), was considered; rejected because the resulting fragments would share the same register and geographic frame as the material on both sides, with no independent scene or transaction marking either as a complete unit on its own - the content-uniformity argument, not an absent seam, is what holds this span together.

boundary_rationale: Opens with an explicit subject reset to a new tribe ('The children of Benjamin didn't drive out the Jebusites') and closes with the etiological 'to this day' formula anchoring Jebusite cohabitation in Jerusalem. The following verse also opens with an explicit subject reset marked by 'also,' confirming this boundary from both sides. Also disclosed: the 'could not drive out' formula family occurs in three principled configurations across this chapter - absorbed as a subordinate clause within a mixed-content register at 1:19 (M8-Judg-005), isolated here at 1:21 because the etiological 'to this day' closure is unique to this verse (and to v26) within the chapter, and gathered whole as a uniform six-entry register at 1:27-36 (M8-Judg-008) because none of those entries carries that etiological closure at all.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Attaching v21 to the tribal-failure register at 1:27-36 was considered as thematically tidier; rejected on a corrected and stronger ground than previously stated: 'ad hayyom hazzeh' does not occur anywhere in 1:27-36 (verified verse by verse), so the register shares only the bare 'didn't drive out' clause with v21, not the etiological 'to this day' closure that is unique in this chapter to v21 and v26 - a textual basis for isolation, not merely an editorial preference. The intervening Joseph/Bethel narrative (22-26) also makes the two failure notices non-contiguous.

parashah_two_witness: samekh after Judg.1.21 (weak corroboration, Prophets)

boundary_rationale: Opens with a subject reset marked by 'also' ('The house of Joseph also went up against Bethel, and Yahweh was with them'), echoing the divine-presence formula of v19 for a new tribe/campaign, and unfolds a discrete spy-and-mercy type-scene (watchers questioned, entrance shown, household spared) paralleling Rahab's episode in Joshua and the Danite spies of ch18. Closes with the etiological naming formula 'which is its name to this day' for the man's new city, Luz. v27 pivots to a formulaic register (tribes failing to dispossess Canaanites) sharing no participants with this scene.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding Manasseh's failure (v27) into this same complex, since both concern incomplete possession, was considered; rejected because v27 lacks the narrative/dialogue texture of 22-26 and instead opens an unrelated formulaic register.

web:Judg.1.26 The man went into the land of the Hittites, built a city, and called its name Luz, which is its name to this day.

boundary_rationale: A uniform-content register of tribes failing to dispossess Canaanite populations (Manasseh, Ephraim, Zebulun, Asher, Naphtali, Dan/Amorites), each sharing the 'X didn't drive out the inhabitants of Y' formula. The prior claim that the entries carry 'no discrete per-entry closure device' is false and withdrawn: each entry does end in a repeated closure clause (yashav be-qerev / la-mas / lo horisho), and every one of the six entry-ends carries an independent parashah mark - samekh after v28 (Manasseh), v30 (Zebulun), v32 (Asher), v33 (Naphtali), and pe after v29 (Ephraim) and v36 (Dan/Amorite border) - six of the six, a perfect correspondence, not the five-of-six previously reported. Tested against that stronger counter-case, the register is still kept whole, on a corrected ground: these closure clauses are content internal to each entry's own reporting sentence, not a separable formal envelope of the kind the minor-judges register carries as a distinct, appended death-and-burial tag (contrast M8-Judg-081/082). None of the six entries here has a scene, speech act, or participant beyond the tribe named at its own opening, so the register-closure criterion, correctly applied, does not force a split even though, as now disclosed in full, every entry-end independently carries a weak Prophets mark. Opens at v27 with the shift into this formulaic register and closes with the summary Amorite border note (v36), the chapter's final verse.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting each tribal entry into its own decision under the register-closure criterion, since all six of the six entry-ends now carry disclosed weak corroboration (samekh at 28/30/32/33, pe at 29/36), was considered; rejected because the closure clauses are content-internal to each entry's own sentence rather than a separable structural tag comparable to the minor-judges' death-and-burial notice, and no entry contains a scene, speech act, or participant of its own beyond the tribe it names - a conclusion now tested against, and holding up against, the full six-of-six correspondence rather than a partial one.

oshb:Judg.1.36 וּגְבוּל֙ הָאֱמֹרִ֔י

boundary_rationale: Opens with a sharp scene shift-new speaker (Yahweh's angel), new movement ('came up from Gilgal to Bochim')-breaking decisively from the tribal conquest register of ch1. The angel's covenant-lawsuit speech (recounting the exodus, the covenant, Israel's failure to obey) runs through v3's judgment sentence. Closes with a discrete two-part etiological notice: naming plus cult ('called the name of that place Bochim...and they sacrificed there to Yahweh,' v5). v6 reopens with a different temporal frame resuming material from Joshua's ending, not continuing the Bochim scene.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending through v6 as one continuous introduction was considered, since both concern the settlement generation; rejected because v6's abrupt pivot to Joshua's dismissal of the people, with no bridge from the weeping and sacrifice of v5, signals a fresh literary unit built on resumptive repetition of Joshua's ending.

oshb:Judg.2.5 וַֽיִּקְרְא֛וּ שֵֽׁם הַמָּק֥וֹם הַה֖וּא בֹּכִ֑ים וַיִּזְבְּחוּ שָׁ֖ם לַֽיהוָֽה

web:Judg.2.5 They called the name of that place Bochim, and they sacrificed there to Yahweh.
parashah_two_witness: pe after Judg.2.1 and after Judg.2.5 (weak corroboration, Prophets - the terminal mark aligns with this span's own close)

boundary_rationale: Opens with an unmistakable Wiederaufnahme-'Now when Joshua had sent the people away, the children of Israel each went to his inheritance to possess the land'-repeating, almost verbatim, the close of Josh.24.28-31 (Joshua's dismissal of the people, his death at 110, burial at Timnath Heres, the generation that outlived him). This resumption signals the narrator restarting the clock after the Bochim aside to open a fresh, more theological retrospective. Closes with the generational turn ('another generation arose after them who didn't know Yahweh,' v10), the pivot into the cyclical description that follows.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading this as mere continuity with 2:1-5, per the general principle that resumptive repetition marks continuity rather than a new unit, was considered; rejected because here the resumption reaches backward across the Joshua/Judges book seam rather than within one scene, so its function is to open a fresh interpretive unit inside Judges even though its content is deliberately repetitive.

literature_type_guess: theological description of the judges-cycle pattern
boundary_rationale: Opens with the first occurrence in Judges of the 'did evil in Yahweh's sight' formula, but used here in its general, iterative sense-describing the recurring apostasy-oppression-judge-relapse pattern rather than instantiating one specific judge's story. The unit elaborates the mechanism in repeatable verbs ('whenever Yahweh raised up judges...when the judge was dead, they turned back') and closes at v19's climactic description of hardened apostasy ('did not cease...or give up their stubborn ways'). v20 shifts into Yahweh's own direct first-person speech, replacing third-person description.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting at v16/17 (the raising of judges) from v18/19 (the pattern of relapse) was considered; rejected because the passage is one continuous description with no participant or scene change, only a sustained iterative argument building to its climax.

oshb:Judg.2.19 לֹ֤א הִפִּ֨ילוּ֙ מִמַּ֣עַלְלֵיהֶ֔ם וּמִדַּרְכָּ֖ם הַקָּשָֽׁה
web:Judg.2.11 The children of Israel did that which was evil in Yahweh's sight, and served the Baals.
web:Judg.2.19 They didn't cease what they were doing, or give up their stubborn ways.

literature_type_guess: divine judicial speech and narrator summary
boundary_rationale: Opens on the discourse shift into first-person divine speech ('I also will no longer drive out...that I may test Israel'), a different mode from the third-person iterative description of 11-19. Note for the record: the anger-formula 'Yahweh's anger burned against Israel' that also appears in this verse is not itself a fresh signal - the identical clause opens 2:14 (inside the preceding span) and recurs at 3:8 (inside the Othniel span), with no subject reset at any of the three sites, so it carries no boundary weight on its own and is not the stated driver here. Closes with the narrator's summary notice ('So Yahweh left those nations, without driving them out hastily'), supplying the premise the following itemized nations-list will expand.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Merging this with 3:1-6 into one span, since both develop the identical 'test' rationale in closely resumptive wording, was considered; rejected because 3:1 opens with the distinct Hebrew list-formula 'these are the nations' (וְאֵלֶּה הַגּוֹיִם), a registral marker beginning a fresh itemized catalogue rather than continuing Yahweh's speech.

oshb:Judg.2.20 וַיֹּ֗אמֶר יַעַן֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָבְר֜וּ הַגּ֣וֹי הַזֶּ֗ה
oshb:Judg.3.8 וַיִּֽחַר אַ֤ף יְהוָה֙ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל
oshb:Judg.2.23 וַיַּנַּ֤ח יְהוָה֙ אֶת הַגּוֹיִ֣ם הָאֵ֔לֶּה

literature_type_guess: itemized nations register with intermarriage/idolatry notice
boundary_rationale: Opens with the formulaic list-introducer 'Now these are the nations which Yahweh left' (וְאֵלֶּה הַגּוֹיִם), a fresh registral marker distinct from the divine speech preceding it, itemizing the five Philistine lords, Canaanites, Sidonians, and Hivites (v3), restating the testing purpose (v4, echoing 2:22), then pivoting to intermarriage and serving 'their gods' (v5-6). Closes at v6's idolatry notice, immediately followed by the unmistakable cyclical 'did evil' formula opening Othniel's cycle at 3:7.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating 2:20-3:6 as one Wiederaufnahme-linked unit, since 'to test Israel' recurs at 2:22, 3:1, and 3:4, was considered; rejected because the list-formula at 3:1 marks a genre shift from direct divine speech to narrator-voiced catalogue, a stronger internal signal than the repeated phrase alone-even though the chapter break itself carries no evidentiary weight.

boundary_rationale: The complete Othniel cycle - sin, servitude under Cushan-Rishathaim, Israel's cry, the raising of Othniel, the Spirit's empowerment, victory, and the closing rest-and-death formula - is bounded entirely by its own framework formulas with no separable narrative content between them. Opens on the pivot from the nations-register of 3:1-6 into cyclical narrative; closes before 3:12 reopens the identical sin-formula with 'again.' Both of this unit's edges now carry disclosed external corroboration: the closing edge's pe after 3:11 (corrected from samekh this round) is joined by an opening-edge witness previously uncited - a pe also falls after 3:6, exactly at this unit's own opening seam - so the HIGH grade here rests on both edges evidenced, not one disclosed and one silent. CYCLE-CLOSE FAMILY RULE, stated here for the family this decision anchors: this campaign isolates a cycle's rest/subdue-and-rest closing formula as its own decision only when it stands alone, undiluted, in its own verse (the paradigm case is Ehud's 3:30, M8-Judg-020). It stays absorbed into the larger unit that precedes it in two other, distinct configurations: when the formula is fused with a death notice in the very same verse with no separable narrative between them, as here (3:11, Othniel's death and the rest-notice share one clause-chain, and the whole five-verse unit is formula throughout with nothing to peel it from); and when verse-level granularity forces the formula into a poem's own closing stanza (5:31, Deborah's Song; M8-Judg-039). These are three different textual configurations governed by one stated policy, not three inconsistent applications of the same rule.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating the whole double introduction (2:6-3:11) as one continuous theological unit was considered; rejected because 3:7 marks the formula's first use to narrate an individually named deliverance rather than describe the pattern abstractly.

boundary_rationale: Opens with the sin-formula repeated with emphatic 'again' and a doubled clause ('did evil...because they had done that which was evil'), distinct wording from Othniel's terser version, followed by Eglon's coalition campaign (Ammon and Amalek, v13) and the eighteen-year servitude notice (v14). Closes with the cry-and-deliverer-raised formula naming Ehud plus the establishing detail of his cover mission ('sent tribute by him to Eglon'), which the following unit's action depends on. v16 pivots from formula to a concrete, sequential action ('Ehud made himself a sword'), opening the assassination narrative proper.
strongest_rejected_alternative: A case could be made for running the setup all the way to v19, tribute delivery included; it loses out because v16 abandons the formulaic register for a specific manufactured object, the sword, opening a scene whose rising tension reads differently from the summary tone of 12-15.

boundary_rationale: Opens with Ehud's concrete preparatory action ('Ehud made himself a sword which had two edges'), a shift from formula to specific object-making, and follows the tribute delivery to 'very fat' Eglon, the dismissal of the tribute-bearers, and Ehud's return with a 'secret message' ploy. Closes with the king's command 'Keep silence!' and the clearing of attendants ('All who stood by him left him')-the private audience the assassination requires is now achieved. v20 opens the private scene proper with Ehud's approach to the seated king.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Closing this unit at v18 (dismissal of the tribute-bearers) rather than v19 was considered; rejected because v19's ruse and the resulting evacuation of attendants is the direct mechanism enabling the assassination, so it belongs with the preparation rather than opening the killing scene itself.

boundary_rationale: Opens with a scene-narrowing shift ('Ehud came to him; and he was sitting by himself alone in the cool upper room'), reducing the cast to just Ehud and Eglon after the attendants' dismissal in v19, and Ehud's 'message from God' pretext leading directly into the stabbing. Closes with Ehud's concealment of the deed (v23), a discrete completed action before the discovery scene begins. GRANULARITY PRINCIPLE, disclosed here and cross-referenced at M8-Judg-019 and M8-Judg-028: Ehud's assassination complex is divided into four decisions (016-019) because each of its scenes carries its own independent formula or scene reset - a manufactured object (016), a cast-narrowing to two named individuals alone (this decision), a Wiederaufnahme establishing simultaneity across a participant change (018), and a battle-summons speech-act to a new addressee (019). Jael's doublet at 4:17-22 (M8-Judg-028) is kept as one span because it supplies no comparable internal marker: it runs as a single continuous action sequence, with no dialogue interruption, from Sisera's flight to Barak's arrival. The two type-scenes are not treated inconsistently; they receive different granularity because the underlying texts supply different numbers of independent internal signals.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending through v25 (the servants' discovery) as one continuous assassination-and-aftermath span was considered; rejected because v24 introduces an entirely new set of participants (the servants) and a new vantage point outside the locked doors, one of the four independent internal resets named above.

boundary_rationale: Opens with new participants, the servants, discovering the locked doors and delaying out of propriety ('Surely he is covering his feet'), then their forced entry and discovery of the body (v25). v26 explicitly reopens the timeline with a resumptive temporal marker ('Ehud escaped while they waited'), signaling that his flight happened during, not after, the servants' delay-a genuine Wiederaufnahme establishing simultaneity, which is why the escape and muster (26-27) are kept with the discovery scene rather than split off. Closes with Ehud leading the mustered Israelites down from the hill country (v27).
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the servants' discovery (24-25) from Ehud's escape and trumpet call (26-27), since they involve different active subjects, was considered; rejected because v26's explicit 'while they waited' back-reference to v25 marks continuity of the same time-span rather than a new scene, matching the campaign's Wiederaufnahme precedent (continuity, not a new unit).

literature_type_guess: battle speech and Jordan fords victory
boundary_rationale: Opens with Ehud's direct battle-summons speech ('Follow me; for Yahweh has delivered your enemies the Moabites into your hand'). Disclosed: the opener wayyomer alehem carries no restated explicit subject and continues an unbroken wayyiqtol chain from v27, so it fails the strict explicit-subject formula-reset test applied elsewhere in this campaign (e.g. 1:3, 4:14). The boundary instead rests on a different, genuine signal: an addressee shift, from Ehud's private pretext-speech to Eglon (closed at 3:19-20's cast-narrowing, M8-Judg-017) to his first recorded speech to the assembled muster - a change of interlocutor and speech-act (private assassination-ruse to public battle-summons) that this campaign treats as boundary-driving independent of the subject-reset test. This is one of the four internally-marked scenes making up Ehud's complex, per the granularity principle stated at M8-Judg-017 and cross-referenced at M8-Judg-028. Closes with the totalizing notice 'No man escaped' (v29); v30 shifts register entirely to a summary closing formula.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Merging 3:28-29 into the preceding muster unit (3:24-27) was considered, since the opener supplies no explicit subject; rejected because the addressee shift (from Eglon to the muster) and speech-act shift (from private ruse to public summons) are independent, genuine signals that survive the failed subject-reset test, and this campaign treats addressee change as boundary-driving elsewhere.

boundary_rationale: A single-verse closing formula-'So Moab was subdued that day under the hand of Israel. Then the land had rest eighty years'-structurally paralleling Othniel's closing notice (3:11) and establishing the pattern applied consistently to every subsequent major-judge cycle in this campaign. Opens on the shift from battle-narrative action to summary notice; closes the entire Ehud complex before v31 introduces an unrelated, unframed judge (Shamgar) with no sin/servitude/cry apparatus at all.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Attaching this verse to 3:28-29 as the battle's natural coda was considered; rejected in favor of treating framework-closing formulas as their own decision consistently across cycles, matching the treatment given to Gideon's parallel notice at 8:28.

boundary_rationale: A single-verse notice for Shamgar the son of Anath, structurally anomalous: no sin-formula opens it, no servitude/cry/rest formula surrounds it, and no death-and-burial closes it, unlike either the major-judge cycles or the minor-judges register of 10:1-5 and 12:8-15. It simply reports the exploit ('struck six hundred men of the Philistines with an ox goad') and a summary verdict ('He also saved Israel'), sandwiched between Ehud's closing formula and ch4's fresh sin-formula opening the Deborah/Barak cycle.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Attaching Shamgar to the Ehud complex as its coda, since both close with 'saved Israel' language, was considered; rejected because 3:30 already supplies Ehud's own complete closing formula, and Shamgar is introduced with 'After him' and an entirely new name, weapon, and single-verse compass, marking him as a distinct, if minimal, entry rather than an appendage.

boundary_rationale: Opens with the sin-formula tied explicitly to Ehud's death ('did that which was evil...when Ehud was dead'), a causal hinge distinct from the bare 'again' of earlier cycles, then the sale into Jabin/Sisera's hand and the twenty-year iron-chariot oppression. Closes with the bare cry-formula ('The children of Israel cried to Yahweh,' v3), before v4 pivots to introduce Deborah by name and title rather than continuing the formula.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending through v4 to fold Deborah's introduction into the same formulaic unit, since she is arguably 'raised up' by this cry, was considered; rejected because the text withholds the raising-up verb here-Deborah is introduced descriptively ('Now Deborah...judged Israel at that time') rather than with the 'Yahweh raised up' verb used for Othniel and Ehud, a deliberate difference in how this unit opens.

boundary_rationale: Opens with a descriptive introduction rather than a raising-up formula ('Now Deborah, a prophetess, the wife of Lappidoth, judged Israel at that time'), and closes with the notice of her judicial seat under the palm tree between Ramah and Bethel, where Israelites came up to her 'for judgment' (v5)-a complete biographical-office notice. v6 shifts to a new action ('She sent and called Barak'), opening direct engagement with the military crisis.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Merging this with 4:6-7 as one continuous 'introduction of the judge and her first act' was considered; rejected because v4-5 is purely descriptive/static (office, location, practice) while v6 initiates a new, dated action with a named addressee-a clear scene-opening shift.

boundary_rationale: Opens with Deborah's summons ('She sent and called Barak the son of Abinoam out of Kedesh Naphtali') and her relayed divine command in direct quotation ('Hasn't Yahweh...commanded, Go and lead the way to Mount Tabor...'), closing with the oracle's promise to draw Sisera to the Kishon and deliver him into Barak's hand (v7). v8 opens Barak's reply, a new speaker with a conditional response.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Keeping 6-10 together as one uninterrupted commissioning dialogue was considered; rejected because Barak's conditional reply (v8) and Deborah's rebuke-oracle (v9) form a distinct exchange with its own internal logic (his hesitancy, her sign of a woman's victory) deserving separation from the initial one-way command.

literature_type_guess: commissioning dialogue (Barak's condition, deliverer's oracle) and muster
boundary_rationale: Opens with Barak's conditional reply ('If you will go with me, then I will go'), a new speech-act responding to Deborah's command, and Deborah's rebuke-oracle reassigning the victory's honor to 'a woman's hand' (v9)-the Jael-foreshadowing governing the rest of the chapter. Closes with the muster notice (v10, ten thousand men, Deborah going up with Barak), completing the commissioning before the narrative shifts to the enemy camp.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting v8-9 (dialogue) from v10 (muster) was considered; rejected because v10 is the direct fulfillment of v9's 'Deborah arose, and went with Barak,' with no new speech-formula or scene marker separating them.

boundary_rationale: A single-verse notice about a third party unconnected to Deborah, Barak, or Sisera-Heber the Kenite's separation from his clan and his encampment 'as far as the oak in Zaanannim'-inserted before the battle narrative resumes. Its function is proleptic: it explains, well in advance, why Sisera will later flee specifically to this family's tent (4:17), a foreshadowing device rather than a scene with dialogue or action. Both edges are thin, which is why this receives a lower confidence despite the clear subject-shift that opens it.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Attaching this verse to the following battle unit (12-16) as background color was considered; rejected because v11 has no narrative connection to the mustering or fighting that follows-it only becomes relevant three units later at v17-and keeping it isolated better reflects its function as an authorial aside.

boundary_rationale: Opens with the report to Sisera of Barak's advance to Mount Tabor (v12) and Sisera's mustering of nine hundred iron chariots (v13), a fresh scene at the enemy camp distinct from the Kedesh muster just narrated. Deborah's go-signal speech ('Go; for this is the day...Hasn't Yahweh gone out before you?') opens the battle proper, running through Yahweh's confusing of Sisera's army and Barak's pursuit 'to Harosheth of the Gentiles.' Closes with the totalizing notice 'There was not a man left' (v16), before v17 narrows to Sisera's individual flight.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the muster/report (12-13) from the battle proper (14-16) was considered; rejected because both share the same escalating momentum toward a single battle with no intervening speech-formula reset strong enough to divide them.

boundary_rationale: Opens with a sharp narrowing to a single fugitive ('Sisera fled away on his feet to the tent of Jael'), motivated by the ki-shalom clause supplied within v17 itself (כִּ֣י שָׁל֗וֹם בֵּ֚ין יָבִ֣ין מֶֽלֶךְ חָצ֔וֹר וּבֵ֕ין בֵּ֖ית חֶ֥בֶר הַקֵּינִ֑י), which activates the Heber notice already planted at v11 (M8-Judg-026) rather than being itself a treaty clause - v11 reports only Heber's separation from the Kenites and his encampment near Kedesh, with no shalom vocabulary of its own. Disclosed: this opener is a resumptive repetition of 4:15 (nas be-raglav / wayyanas be-raglav), and the campaign's Wiederaufnahme criterion is applied here as follows - at 3:26, resumption backs the narrative up over a single intervening clause about the same actors in the same scene, establishing simultaneity (continuity, not a new unit); at 4:17, by contrast, the resumption follows v16's scene-ending totalizing notice and redirects the narrative's entire focus onto a different individual in a new location, the same 'redirect-of-focus' pattern that opens a unit at 2:6. This decision's opening at 4:17 is governed by the 2:6 precedent, not the 3:26 precedent. Closes with the visual confirmation 'Sisera lay dead, and the tent peg was in his temples' (v22); v23 shifts to a narrator's summary evaluation.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the hospitality/killing (17-21) from Barak's discovery (22) was considered; rejected because v22 is the scene's dramatic payoff, belonging with the type-scene it completes. Per M8-Judg-017/019, this scene's internal granularity (kept as one span) is itself the contrast case for Ehud's four-way subdivided complex, since Jael's doublet supplies no comparable internal formula/scene reset between the flight and Barak's arrival.

boundary_rationale: Opens with a shift to third-person theological summary ('So God subdued Jabin the king of Canaan'), replacing the scene-level narrative of Jael's tent, and closes with the notice of Israel's escalating dominance 'until they had destroyed Jabin king of Canaan' (v24). Notably this closing lacks the 'land had rest X years' formula used elsewhere, substituting a progressive-defeat notice instead-a variation this campaign discloses rather than forces into the standard mold; the rest-notice for this cycle appears at the end of the Song instead (5:31), reflecting the prose account's deferral to its poetic counterpart.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating 4:23-24 as the final beat of the Jael episode rather than its own closing unit was considered; rejected because the shift from named-participant scene to impersonal theological summary ('God,' not Yahweh; 'the children of Israel' as a collective) marks a register change matching this campaign's cycle-closing treatment elsewhere.

strongest_rejected_alternative: Merging v1 with v2-3 as the poem's opening strophe was considered, since ancient Hebrew poetry sometimes carries its own superscription-line; rejected because the underlying lineation itself marks v1 as unlineated narration and v2 as the first poetic line, an objective form-signal rather than an interpretive judgment.

This decision is narrowed to v2 alone on an undisclosed lexical-refrain signal: the epithet YHWH Elohei Yisrael closes both v3 and v5, its only two occurrences in the Song (full-chapter scan of Judg_oshb.txt), bracketing v3 with the theophany of vv4-5 rather than with v2's summons. The WEB \b stanza dividers after v2 and after v3 are disclosed as symmetric, non-driving metadata under m8-mesh-r2 and do not themselves move the boundary; the epithet bracket is the admissible driver. strongest_rejected_alternative: Keeping vv2-3 merged, as previously drawn, was this decision's own prior position; withdrawn because it grouped v3 with v2's summons-register while separating it from the epithet it shares only with v5, breaking the one lexical bracket the Song supplies for this stretch.

boundary_rationale: Neighbor revision triggered by M8-Judg-031's re-decision (epithet bracket at v3/v5; see that decision for the full evidence). Opens with v3's dedication clause ('I, even I, will sing to Yahweh...the God of Israel'), sharing v2's summons register in its first half but closing on the epithet YHWH Elohei Yisrael that recurs, and only recurs, at v5's theophany climax - an undisclosed lexical bracket binding v3 to the storm-theophany of vv4-5 rather than to v2's outward summons. The theophany proper - direct second-person address to Yahweh, earth trembling, mountains melting, Sinai named - occupies v4-5, framed on its near side by v3's epithet-anticipating dedication. Closes at v5's Sinai-climax and its own use of the bracketing epithet; v6 pivots to a dated historical register ('In the days of Shamgar...in the days of Jael').
strongest_rejected_alternative: Two alternatives are now on record. First, retaining the prior division (v3 grouped with v2, theophany beginning at v4) was this decision's own prior position; withdrawn per the reasons stated at M8-Judg-031 - the epithet bracket at v3/v5 outweighs the WEB \b stanza divider after v3, which is disclosed as non-driving metadata under m8-mesh-r2. Second, and not previously engaged: v2-v3 form a homogeneous block of second-person imperatives addressed to human hearers (בָּרֲכ֖וּ יְהוָֽה to the people generally at v2; שִׁמְע֣וּ מְלָכִ֔ים... הַאֲזִ֖ינוּ רֹֽזְנִ֑ים to kings and princes at v3), while v4 turns to vocative second-person address to Yahweh himself (יְהוָ֗ה בְּצֵאתְךָ֤ מִשֵּׂעִיר֙). Change of addressee is a criterion this campaign treats as decisive elsewhere - M8-Judg-001's rejection of extending into 1:3 on a shift of addressee; M8-Judg-033's own close on a v9 address-and-mood shift - and taken alone it would cut at 3|4, inside this span's own opening rather than at its drawn edge. It is outweighed here because v3 does not merely continue v2's summons register: v3 itself pivots mid-verse from the summons (שִׁמְע֣וּ מְלָכִ֔ים) into the singer's own first-person announcement (אָֽנֹכִ֗י לַֽיהוָה֙ אָנֹכִ֣י אָשִׁ֔ירָה אֲזַמֵּ֕ר לַֽיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל, 'I, even I, will sing to Yahweh... to Yahweh, the God of Israel'), and that announcement's own closing epithet is the one that brackets v5's theophany climax. So v3 both opens with the summons register it shares with v2 and closes already inside the epithet bracket that binds it to v4-5; the addressee reset is real, but it falls inside v3 rather than at its edges, and the unit this decision draws (v3-5) is the one that keeps the epithet-bracketed announcement-and-theophany together rather than splitting the announcement from what it announces.

boundary_rationale: Opens with the dated formula 'In the days of Shamgar the son of Anath, in the days of Jael,' pivoting to a concrete historical description of danger and Israel's military weakness. The prior closing rationale - a contrast between 'third-person historical description' in 6-8 and 'first-person' in 9-11 - is false as stated and withdrawn: v7 contains shaqqamti twice, first-person qatal forms ('until I, Deborah, arose'). The close at v8 is retained on a corrected ground: v8 ends a rhetorical question about disarmament ('Was there a shield or spear seen...?'), and v9 opens a genuine mood/address shift, from lament-question to praise-refrain ('My heart is toward the governors...Bless Yahweh!'). Disclosed as a counter-signal: WEB's \b stanza divider runs vv6-9 as one unbroken strophe, with the next break falling only after v9, so the poem's own formatting does not mark this seam; per m8-mesh-r2 this non-driving metadata does not override the text-level mood shift but is recorded rather than concealed.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating 6-11 as a single crisis-and-resolution unit remains on the table in principle, since the poem's own \b lineation runs unbroken across 6-9 - a counter-signal disclosed here rather than hidden. Still, v9 turns from v8's disarmament-question to a mood of praise ('Bless Yahweh!'), enough of an address shift, however modest, to hold the seam at v8.

This campaign's units are not drawn at sub-verse granularity, so this mid-verse seam does not itself relocate the close at v11, but it is disclosed rather than concealed. Both edges are marked by a shift in address-mode, direct second-person imperative to named individuals bracketed on either side by third-person/communal narration, though the verse's brevity limits confidence.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Attaching this verse to the tribal-muster catalogue (13-18) as its heading was considered, since the muster answers this call; rejected because v12's mode is direct apostrophe to named individuals while v13 shifts to third-person description of tribes as a class, a distinct enough form to isolate the summons.

boundary_rationale: Opens with the battle's combatants named directly ('The kings came and fought, then the kings of Canaan fought at Taanach'), cosmic imagery of stars fighting from their courses, and the Kishon's sweeping flood, closing with the messenger-formula curse 'Curse Meroz, said Yahweh's angel...because they didn't come to help Yahweh against the mighty' (v23), a discrete imprecation with its own speech-formula. v24 pivots from cursing to blessing, addressing Jael by name. Lineation evidence, previously undisclosed: WEB's own stanza dividers (\b) fall after v18 and after v23, with none in between - so 19-23 reads as one unbroken strophe in the translation's own structure, corroborating (as non-driving metadata under m8-mesh-r2) the decision to keep the Meroz curse inside this unit rather than isolating it.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Keeping the Meroz curse (v23) as its own single-verse unit, separate from the battle description, was considered and rejected on two grounds. First, the curse functions as the battle account's rhetorical conclusion, naming the coalition's one conspicuous absence, tightly bound to the preceding combat imagery rather than standing independently - the ground previously stated, which by itself did not engage the strongest form of the alternative. Second, and now engaged directly: v23 opens with a quotative frame embedded inside the curse itself (אָמַר֙ מַלְאַ֣ךְ יְהוָ֔ה, 'said Yahweh's angel'), reporting the imprecation as another speaker's words within the poem, in contrast to 5:12's own unit-opening imperatives (עוּרִי עוּרִי דְּבוֹרָה, 'Awake, awake, Deborah'), which address a named individual directly with no embedded quotative frame. That contrast could support reading v23 as a distinct speech-act rather than the narrating voice's own rhetorical close; it is outweighed here because the quotative frame reports the angel's curse as part of the same battle-song's continuous voice rather than introducing a speaker external to it (contrast the shift to Deborah's own summons voice at 5:12, which does open a new unit), and because the lineation evidence now disclosed above - one unbroken strophe from v19 to v23 - corroborates keeping the two together.

boundary_rationale: Opens with a direct shift from imprecation to blessing, marked by the antithetical formula 'Jael shall be blessed above women...blessed shall she be above women in the tent,' a deliberate structural counterpoint to the Meroz curse it immediately follows. Narrates the hospitality-then-killing sequence in poetic replay (milk, hammer, tent peg) and closes with the visual tableau of Sisera's collapse, 'where he bowed, there he fell down dead' (v27). v28 shifts scene entirely to Sisera's household, a new location and cast.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this unit through v31 as one continuous 'Jael and aftermath' span was considered; rejected because v28 opens a wholly new scene-different location, new characters, ironic dramatic distance-that functions as this poem's counter-scene to Jael's triumph, warranting its own boundary.

literature_type_guess: ironic counter-scene, curse/blessing coda, and cycle-closing rest formula
boundary_rationale: Opens with a scene-shift to Sisera's household ('Through the window she looked out, and cried: Sisera's mother looked through the lattice'), an ironic counter-scene to Jael's tent in which the anticipated victory-plunder never arrives, closing with the poem's final imprecation/blessing couplet ('So let all your enemies perish, Yahweh, but let those who love him be as the sun...,' v31a). The verse then continues, within the same versification, into a prose-register notice, 'Then the land had rest forty years' (v31b), marked in the underlying text by the drop out of q1/q2 poetic lineation into unmarked narration-a poem/prose transition. Because span granularity is fixed at the verse level, this decision necessarily includes both the poem's climactic couplet and the cycle-closing rest formula in one span; the rest-notice is disclosed here as functioning as the cyclical framework's closing bookend (paralleling Othniel 3:11, Ehud 3:30) grafted directly onto the Song's final line, integrating ch5 into the same framework used for the prose cycles rather than standing outside it. A WEB stanza divider (\b) falls after v30, interior to this span; disclosed here as a genuine counter-signal to any reading of 28-31 as one seamless poetic sweep, though as non-driving metadata under m8-mesh-r2 it does not itself relocate the boundary, which remains fixed at the verse level regardless.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating v31 as its own single-verse decision separate from 28-30, isolating the seam where poetry gives way to the framework-closing prose, was considered; rejected because verse-level granularity does not allow splitting within v31. The curse/blessing couplet of 31a is the poetic resolution of Sisera's mother's foiled hope in 28-30, but the reading is stated more cautiously than 'one continuous arc': a WEB stanza divider falls after v30, interior to this span, marking 28-30 and 31a as formally distinct strophes even as they remain thematically continuous - taunt-and-foiled-hope, then triumph-and-rest, rather than one unbroken sweep. The disclosed interior break does not itself move the boundary, fixed at the verse level, but it tempers the unity claim to what the evidence actually supports.

boundary_rationale: Opens with the men of Israel's dynastic kingship offer ('Rule over us, both you, your son, and your son's son also') and closes with Gideon's theocratic refusal, 'Yahweh shall rule over you' (v23). Both v23 and the following v24 open with the identical explicit-subject speech formula wayyomer alehem gid'on, identical in consonants and vocalization; the three accents differ (mahapakh against qadma on the verb, pashta against geresh on the prepositional phrase, zaqef qatan against revia on the name), a cantillation-level difference this campaign's deterministic sweep, which strips combining marks by design, is not built to catch and does not claim to audit - framing a maximal content shift from theocratic refusal to a request for plunder. Under the explicit-subject formula-reset principle applied throughout this campaign (e.g. M8-Judg-001), an identical formula reset with a total content shift opens a new unit; this decision is narrowed to the refusal alone, with the ephod episode split off as its own sibling decision, M8-Judg-175.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Keeping vv22-27 as one continuous scene, on the ground that the juxtaposition of noble refusal with idolatrous aftermath is itself the passage's literary point, was this decision's own prior position; withdrawn because the explicit-subject formula-reset principle, applied consistently elsewhere in this campaign, is not suspended merely because a rhetorical effect depends on adjacency - the irony survives the split, since the two decisions still sit next to each other in sequence. The WEB paragraph evidence (no break between 8:23 and 8:24, with breaks present before 8:23 and before 8:25) is disclosed as genuine corroboration for the prior merge, but under this mesh's rule hierarchy WEB paragraphing is non-driving corroboration and cannot outrank a text signal.

literature_type_guess: diplomatic correspondence, historical-legal brief, and its failure
boundary_rationale: Neighbor revision triggered by the left-edge question filed at M8-Judg-092 (LF-M8-Judg-092-frontier_defer). Opens with the second embassy's messenger-formula and Jephthah's historical-legal brief, delivered as one continuous, uninterrupted speech. Closes with the appeal to divine arbitration, 'May Yahweh the Judge be judge today...' (v27), and extends one verse further to the narrator's report that the appeal failed: 'the king of the children of Ammon didn't listen to the words of Jephthah which he sent him' (v28). v28's grammatical subject (melekh benei ammon, 'the king of the children of Ammon') continues this brief's antagonist rather than introducing anything new, and its content explicitly back-references the messengers Jephthah sent at v14 ('the words of Jephthah...which he sent'), making it this unit's own closing failure-notice rather than the next unit's opening premise. The only external mark at this edge is the agreed pe after 11:28, and under this campaign's standing rule that Prophets marks are weak corroboration that never drive or lift a grade, it cannot itself carry the HIGH here - disclosed as such rather than leaned on. Against it, WEB's own paragraph index runs the other way and is disclosed here rather than passed over: it opens a paragraph at v28 and none at v29, grouping 28 with 29 (the same pattern M8-Judg-092, revised, records for this seam) - a genuine counter-signal, though itself non-driving metadata under m8-mesh-r2. What actually carries this closing edge is the content shift the reset marks: v28 ends this brief's own register, the human diplomatic failure ('the king of the children of Ammon didn't listen'), and v29 opens a wholly different one, divine empowerment ('the Spirit of Yahweh came upon Jephthah'), with a clean explicit-subject reset - the kind this campaign treats as decisive elsewhere (e.g. M8-Judg-001, M8-Judg-061) - a text-internal signal admissible in its own right, independent of either disclosed external mark.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Keeping v28 with the following unit, as this campaign previously drew the line - reading the failure-notice as the direct causal hinge into the following military and votive action - was reconsidered under the left-edge question formally filed at M8-Judg-092 (LF frontier_defer). Resolved here toward binding v28 to this decision: the subject-continuity with 'the king of the children of Ammon,' the explicit back-reference to 'the words of Jephthah...sent,' and the independently corroborating parashah pe after v28 together outweigh the causal-momentum reading, under the explicit-subject formula-reset principle applied consistently elsewhere in this campaign.

boundary_rationale: MERGE (round-3 micro-authoring): this decision now absorbs M8-Judg-176 (previously Judg.11.30-11.31, the vow), which is retired and superseded into this span; see _meta.merges. Opens with the explicit-subject reset 'the Spirit of Yahweh came upon Jephthah' (v29), the direct sequel to the diplomatic brief's failure now closed off at M8-Judg-091 (revised to include v28, whose own closing edge this same reset corroborates). Narrates his advance through Gilead and Manasseh, Mizpah of Gilead, and onward to the Ammonites (v29b), then his votive speech-act, 'Jephthah vowed a vow to Yahweh, and said' (v30, וַיִּדַּ֨ר יִפְתָּ֥ח נֶ֛דֶר לַיהוָ֖ה וַיֹּאמַ֑ר), quoting the conditional terms in full, and the vow's completion (v31). CYCLE PRECEDENT: this campaign does not isolate the Spirit-of-Yahweh empowerment formula as its own decision anywhere else it occurs - at 3:10 (M8-Judg-014) it is folded into the whole Othniel cycle unit (3:7-11), and at 15:14 (M8-Judg-120) it is folded into the battle-and-etiology unit (15:14-17) alongside Samson's own direct-speech boast and its naming aftermath. Both of those units carry real internal content variety - battle narration next to a formulaic death notice at 3:7-11, combat next to a victory-boast and an etiological naming at 15:14-17 - and still stay whole because the empowerment is treated as the hinge that starts the action it triggers, not a scene standing on its own. The same pattern governs here: v29's empowerment triggers the itinerary that closes the verse, and the itinerary's arrival at the Ammonites is what the vow (v30) responds to, its own explicit-subject formula and genre shift into legal/votive speech notwithstanding - a content shift of the same kind the 3:7-11 and 15:14-17 units already absorb without splitting. WITNESS EVIDENCE, corrected: the parashah tradition's pe after 11:28 and pe after 11:31 bracket this span exactly, yielding one 11:29-11:31 section, not the isolated-v29 reading this decision previously drew from the same file while citing the identical marks - that self-contradiction is withdrawn. WEB's paragraph index opens a break before v30, interior to this span (disclosed as a genuine counter-signal, non-driving metadata under m8-mesh-r2), but none before v29 or before v32, so the span's own outer edges carry no WEB counter-evidence. Closes at v31's completion of the vow; v32 opens the battle's execution, already the opening of the existing M8-Judg-093, unaffected by this merge.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Two prior positions are both withdrawn here. First, this campaign's earliest position - keeping vv28-31 as one continuous unit - is withdrawn because v28 is bound backward to M8-Judg-091 on independent grounds stated there (subject-continuity with the antagonist, the explicit back-reference to v14, and the empowerment reset itself as the closing edge's driver). Second, this decision's own immediately prior position - isolating v29 alone and splitting the vow into a separate sibling (M8-Judg-176) - is also withdrawn, on the 3:10/15:14 precedent stated above and on a corrected reading of the witnesses: the two parashah marks this decision itself discloses (pe after 11:28, pe after 11:31) converge on grouping v29 with v30-31, not on isolating v29, and the further split from v30 rested only on an internal-consistency argument borrowed from M8-Judg-093's stated practice of separating speech-acts from summary notices - a legitimate methodological tool elsewhere, but not independent evidence at this seam, and not sufficient on its own to override both the witnessed grouping and the empowerment-formula precedent. The WEB break before v30 is disclosed as a real, if non-driving, counter-signal favoring the narrower split; it does not outweigh the convergence of the other two considerations.

boundary_rationale: Unchanged in substance. Opens with the muster and battle proper (12:4) triggered by Ephraim's taunt, and narrates the Shibboleth checkpoint (5-6) as the battle's direct continuation, closing on the casualty tally.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Two alternatives were tested. (a) Separating the battle proper (v4) from the checkpoint scene (5-6): rejected because the checkpoint is the battle's resolution, seizing the fords as part of the same engagement, with no scene-break between combat and pursuit. (b) Reading Judg.12.1-6 as a single Ephraim-quarrel unit on the model of Gideon's Ephraim exchange at 8:1-3 (decision M8-Judg-096 covers 12:1-3): both units open with an Ephraimite grievance framed as a question answered by the judge in the first person (12:1 מַדּ֣וּעַ; 8:1 מָֽה הַדָּבָ֤ר הַזֶּה֙) - a genuine structural family. But the outcomes diverge: 8:1-3 resolves entirely in Gideon's placating speech, with the narrative moving straight to his own pursuit of Midian and no battle against Ephraim following; 12:1-3 instead ends on Jephthah's own unanswered rhetorical question, לְהִלָּחֵ֥ם בִּֽי ('to fight against me'), which 12:4 then answers with actual bloodshed. The two units are cousins in form, not twins in outcome, and that divergence is the reason 096/097 stays split from the 8:1-3 pairing rather than merging into one Ephraim-quarrel span.

strongest_rejected_alternative: Attaching this verse to the Shibboleth battle unit (097) as its coda was considered; rejected in favor of treating tenure-and-death closing formulas as their own decision when they can be cleanly peeled from surrounding narrative, matching the treatment of Ehud (3:30) and Gideon (8:28). literature_type_guess: retaliation scene (Philistines burn the wife and father)
boundary_rationale: A single-verse but self-contained exchange - the Philistines' own inquiry, identification of Samson's motive, and retaliation, burning 'her and her father with fire' - between Samson's arson (3-5) and his counter-retaliation (7-8). Both edges are explicit-subject speech resets, and both are doubly attested: וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ פְלִשְׁתִּים֮ opens this verse with a new collective subject (also marked by a WEB paragraph break before 15:6), and וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לָהֶם֙ שִׁמְשׁ֔וֹן opens the next unit (118) by restoring Samson as speaker (also marked by a WEB paragraph break before 15:7). Single-verse scope is not by itself a confidence criterion in this map - six other single-verse decisions stand at HIGH (M8-Judg-006 at 1:21, M8-Judg-020 at 3:30, M8-Judg-098 at 12:7, M8-Judg-122 at 15:20, M8-Judg-134 at 16:31, M8-Judg-160 at 20:18) - so it is dropped as a ground here; the text-internal formula reset at both edges is what carries the grade, corroborated but not driven by the disclosed paragraph evidence.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Two alternatives are now on record. (a) Folding this verse into the preceding foxes-and-torches unit (116) was considered and rejected: v6 introduces an entirely new scene with the Philistines as actors and speakers, formally distinct from Samson's own action-narrative in 3-5. (b) Folding this verse forward into the following unit (118, Judg.15.7-8) was also tested and rejected: v6 opens on its own explicit-subject reset (וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ פְלִשְׁתִּים) and 15:7 opens on its own, different explicit-subject reset (וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לָהֶם֙ שִׁמְשׁ֔וֹן) - folding v6 into 118 would require overriding a clean formula-reset at both of the verse's edges, against the campaign's own explicit-subject-reset criterion. The verse is retained as its own decision on that ground.

boundary_rationale: Opens with Samson's arrival at Lehi, cited from its true head: הוּא בָ֣א עַד לֶ֔חִי, an independent pronoun fronted before a qatal - a genuine scene-transition construction distinct from the surrounding wayyiqtol chain - followed by the Spirit-empowerment formula that frees him from his bonds, his improvised jawbone weapon, and its use against a thousand men, including his own victory-boast couplet (v16). The couplet has real parallelism and wordplay (בִּלְחִ֣י הַחֲמ֔וֹר חֲמ֖וֹר חֲמֹרָתָ֑יִם on לֶחִי/חֲמוֹר) but is set as ordinary prose accentuation in the workspace source, not poetic |q1/|q2 lineation - that specific claim is withdrawn; the campaign's |q1/|q2 markers occur only at 14:14 and 14:18 across chapters 11-17. Closes with the etiological naming of Ramath Lehi (v17), which explicitly derives from the boast's own vocabulary (וַֽיְהִי֙ כְּכַלֹּת֣וֹ לְדַבֵּ֔ר, a clause subordinating itself to the speech just given and therefore unable to head a unit). v18 opens Samson's thirst and prayer, a new physical need.

boundary_rationale: Opens with Samson's sudden thirst and prayer of complaint, contrasting his victory with the indignity of dying of thirst 'and fall into the hands of the uncircumcised' (וְעַתָּה֙ אָמ֣וּת בַּצָּמָ֔א), and narrates God's answer at Lehi. Closes with the etiological naming of En Hakkore and the durative 'to this day' formula (v19), a genuinely strong right edge. v20 shifts entirely to the tenure-closing formula. The left edge (15:18) is honestly weaker than previously disclosed: it is a bare wayyiqtol continuing the same actor from 15:17 with no expressed subject, no fronted clause, no temporal marker, and - now that the fabricated pe is removed - no parashah mark of any kind (ch15's marks are the samekh after 15:8 and the pe after 15:20; nothing at 15:17|15:18). A WEB paragraph break does open at 15:18, disclosed here as the same class of non-driving metadata cited at dozens of other edges in this map, not as an independent text signal. What actually carries the seam is a register change (triumph to physical need) and the closural force of the etiology that follows, not any independent text signal on this edge.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Two alternatives are now on record. (a) Folding v20 into this unit as its natural coda was considered and rejected; v20's bare tenure formula has no narrative continuity to the spring-miracle scene, and closing formulas are treated as their own decision consistently across cycles. (b) Merging 15:18-19 back into M8-Judg-120 so that the whole Lehi episode, with its two etiologies, stands as one span was not previously tested and is now argued honestly: the subject continues unbroken across 15:17/15:18, and both etiologies are built on the same toponym לֶחִי, with the second explicitly anchored אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּלֶּ֔חִי - real support for the merge. Against it stands the register change from triumphant boast to physical crisis, and the fact that a divine petition and its answer intervene between the two namings, which is a genuine scene of its own rather than a mere continuation. The drafted split is retained on that balance, but honestly as a closer call than the original medium rating disclosed, and the left edge's lack of independent corroboration is now stated plainly rather than papered over with an invented mark.

boundary_rationale: Opens with Delilah's third accusation-and-request, now specifying 'until now' the pattern of deception, and Samson's answer involving the loom. Closes with his effortless escape (v14). The right edge against the fourth round (128, beginning 16:15) is honestly the softer of this unit's two edges: 16:15 opens with only וַתֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֗יו, lacking the full nominal frame (וַתֹּאמֶר דְּלִילָה אֶל שִׁמְשׁוֹן) that opens rounds one through three at 16:6, 16:10, and 16:13 - the explicit-subject-reset criterion used to separate the first three rounds from each other does not, by itself, separate the third from the fourth. The seam is retained on a different, stated ground: register-closure. Rounds one through three are formally half-truths of escalating specificity (cords, ropes, loom) narrated at the same distance, and the accusation that opens each later round is not a clean break between them: round three's own opening (עַד הֵ֜נָּה הֵתַ֤לְתָּ בִּי֙ וַתְּדַבֵּ֤ר אֵלַי֙ כְּזָבִ֔ים, 16:13) repeats round two's wording (הִנֵּה֙ הֵתַ֣לְתָּ בִּ֔י וַתְּדַבֵּ֥ר אֵלַ֖י כְּזָבִ֑ים, 16:10) almost verbatim, and round four's own opening (זֶ֣ה שָׁלֹ֤שׁ פְּעָמִים֙ הֵתַ֣לְתָּ בִּ֔י, 16:15) explicitly tallies back across that same הֵתַלְתָּ בִּי root rather than introducing a new one - honestly disclosed here as a continuous accusation-thread running from round two through round four, a crescendo rather than a clean two-part structure. Register-closure is retained as the ground for this seam regardless: what changes at round four is not the accusation itself (which round four inherits and merely counts) but everything downstream of it - round four alone abandons the request-and-material exchange pattern (cords, ropes, loom, each answered with a fabricated countermeasure) for sustained emotional pressure (daily nagging, 'his soul was troubled to death') that finally extracts the real secret, a shift in the scene's own mechanism, not in Delilah's opening line. The seam is accordingly the weakest of the four round-boundaries in this unit, resting on that downstream shift alone rather than on any discontinuity in the accusation itself, and is disclosed as such rather than as a clean content break. 16:16's wayehi-plus-durative opener (וַ֠יְהִי כִּֽי הֵצִ֨יקָה לּ֧וֹ בִדְבָרֶ֛יהָ כָּל הַיָּמִ֖ים) is the strongest reset device in the four-round sequence and sits inside the following decision's span rather than at either of its edges; it is disclosed there.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Merging this round with the fourth (15-17) into one span was considered on two grounds and rejected on both, now stated rather than left implicit. First, both concern hair and share Delilah as the continuous acting subject across the seam (וַתִּתְקַע...וַתֹּאמֶר...וַתֹּאמֶר), which argues for continuity; against it, v13-14's material is still a deceptive half-truth like rounds one and two, while 15-17 finally extracts the true Nazirite secret - a content break the campaign treats as licensing a fresh unit for type-scenes with genuine content differentiation. Second, re-cutting the seam one verse later, at 16:15/16:16, to use 16:16's stronger wayehi-plus-durative opener as the boundary instead, was also considered; rejected because it would sever Delilah's reproach (15) from the pressure campaign it inaugurates (16) and from the confession it produces (17), which read as one uninterrupted escalation, and because doing so would only relocate rather than resolve the underlying softness at the third/fourth-round seam.

literature_type_guess: burial notice and cycle tenure-closure (second half of the doubled colophon)
boundary_rationale: A single verse combining Samson's burial with the second occurrence of the tenure-formula. This decision discloses the doubled colophon explicitly rather than resolving it by omission: Samson's tenure is stated twice, once mid-career (15:20) and once at his death (here). The two notices are not verbally identical, and the corrected comparison strengthens rather than weakens the disclosure this decision exists to make: 15:20 uses wayyiqtol with no independent subject and adds 'in the days of the Philistines'; 16:31 uses a fronted independent pronoun (הוּא) plus qatal and omits that phrase. The shared material is limited to אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל, עֶשְׂרִים שָׁנָה, and the root שׁפט. Two structurally different colophon constructions bracket the same twenty-year figure; disclosing that divergence honestly is this decision's task, and the divergence itself is not read here as evidence one way or the other about deliberate design. This book's own comparandum runs the other direction: the refrain this campaign already treats as a deliberate literary bracket, 17:6/21:25 (M8-Judg-174), is byte-identical, cantillation included, and it is that identity, not divergence, that this campaign takes as the signature of an intentional inclusio. The 15:20/16:31 doubling is accordingly disclosed on its own terms - two notices, genuinely different in form, both standing at real narrative pauses - without the further claim that their divergence itself argues for a considered two-panel composition. Closes the entire Samson complex before ch17 opens the appendices with no framework formula at all.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Unchanged in conclusion: treating only this verse as the real closing formula and downgrading 15:20 to a mere narrative aside was considered and rejected; both notices stand at genuine narrative pauses, so privileging one over the other would suppress rather than disclose the doubling this campaign's hard tests require addressing. M8-Judg-122's own phrasing for the same relationship, 'an almost identical notice,' is the accurate formulation and now governs the language used here as well.

The changeover coincides exactly with the drafted boundary. v5 shifts to a summary description of Micah's private shrine.

boundary_rationale: Opens with the short-form refrain at 18:1, whose cohesion with the new Danite subject rests on resumptive repetition of the temporal adverbial (בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֔ם...וּבַיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֗ם), not on the two clauses being grammatically fused into a single continuous sentence - both clauses are independently athnach-divided, the same pausal structure the full-form refrain carries at 17:6 and 21:25. Narrates the dispatch of five spies; closes with their lodging (v2). v3's opening (הֵ֚מָּה עִם בֵּ֣ית מִיכָ֔ה וְהֵ֣מָּה הִכִּ֔ירוּ) is a continuative circumstantial clause naming no new participant and restating the location v2 has just reached, which weakens rather than strengthens this decision's closing edge.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Two alternatives are on record. (a) Treating the refrain (v1a) as its own micro-unit was considered and rejected on the corrected ground of resumptive repetition (not fusion) binding it to the Danite notice. (b) Testing whether 18:1-2 should instead extend through 18:6 (merging with M8-Judg-139) to close on the priest's oracle formula לְכ֣וּ לְשָׁל֑וֹם, where both parashah witnesses register a petuchah, was not previously tested. It is a real competitor - v3's circumstantial opener supplies no independent reset - but is not adopted: M8-Judg-139's own opening (the voice-recognition at 18:3, the first thing in the chapter that is not itinerary) is treated as a genuine scene-trigger in its own right, and collapsing the 138/139 boundary would lose a distinction the campaign protects carefully elsewhere between narration and the report or recognition that reframes it. The span is kept at Judg.18.1-Judg.18.2 with confidence lowered to reflect that its closing edge is soft.

boundary_rationale: A single-verse scene shift to Laish. The opening edge is stronger than previously credited: 18:7 opens וַיֵּלְכוּ֙ חֲמֵ֣שֶׁת הָאֲנָשִׁ֔ים וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ לָ֑יְשָׁה, a full subject respecification after four verses of inflection-only reference, paired with a departure-arrival verb pair reaching a new place - genuine text signals, not merely 'no dialogue.' The closing edge is the one that is honestly weak: 18:8 continues וַיָּבֹ֨אוּ֙ אֶל אֲחֵיהֶ֔ם with no subject respecified and no temporal or spatial reset beyond the next stage of the same itinerary, simply repeating v7's arrival verb for the return leg. The only differentiator is register (third-person narration versus reported speech beginning at v8), and register alone does not carry an edge under this campaign's symmetric-marker-insufficiency principle. No parashah mark falls anywhere in 18:7-10, and WEB in fact runs 18:7-8 together as one paragraph, starting fresh only at 18:9 - external evidence that, if anything, favors folding v7 forward rather than treating it as freestanding.
strongest_rejected_alternative: The merge tested (folding 18:7 down into the report scene, 141) is the wrong one to have relied on alone. The alternative that actually threatens this decision - reading 18:7-10 as one reconnaissance-and-report unit bracketed by the two arrivals (וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ at v7, וַיָּבֹ֨אוּ֙ at v8) - is now tested here honestly. It has real support: no independent text signal separates v7 from v8 beyond register, and WEB's own paragraphing runs the two together. Against it: the report in vv8-10 is explicitly cast as the spies' own reported dialogue to a different audience (their brothers at Zorah and Eshtaol) at a different location, which this campaign treats elsewhere as a genuine narratorial-voice-versus-direct-speech distinction (compare the same distinction protecting 140/141 from 139 above). The span is retained as its own single-verse decision, but the confidence rating's own hedge is now correctly located: it protects against the closing edge's weakness, not against uniform uncertainty across the whole verse.

literature_type_guess: theft narrative (idols taken under armed guard)
boundary_rationale: Opens with the five original spies' proposal to their kinsmen about the ephod, teraphim, and images (18:14), a return to individual speech after the collective muster notice, and narrates the theft while the six hundred armed men and the priest stand guard at the gate. The clause at 18:17 (arrival and taking of the four objects) is picked back up verbatim in structure at 18:18 (וְאֵ֗לֶּה בָּ֚אוּ בֵּ֣ית מִיכָ֔ה וַיִּקְחוּ֙...) after the parenthetical gate-guard aside - a resumptive repetition (Wiederaufnahme) that signals continuity across what the original decisions treated as a boundary, not a fresh start. The priest's challenge (מָ֥ה אַתֶּ֖ם עֹשִֽׂים, 18:18b) sits behind that resumption, and the Danites' counter-offer and his acceptance follow in one unbroken sequence. Closes with the priest's glad assent and his crossing over to join the people (וַיָּבֹ֖א בְּקֶ֥רֶב הָעָֽם, 18:20). v21 turns the whole column around with וַיִּפְנ֖וּ וַיֵּלֵ֑ךְ, a genuine register change to logistics and departure, which is where the next unit (145) already opens. External evidence, previously undisclosed: WEB opens paragraphs at 18:18, 18:19, and 18:20 - the priest's challenge, the Danites' counter-offer, and his acceptance each set off as their own paragraph - but these read as dialogue-turn markers within one continuous exchange rather than section divisions, consistent with the chapter's dense paragraphing elsewhere (18:1, 18:4, 18:5, 18:6, 18:7, 18:9, 18:11, 18:14 are all turn- or beat-level breaks in the same stretch); the next section-level break does not fall until 18:24. The adopted close at 18:20|18:21 itself carries no external witness at all - WEB runs no break there, and the parashah tradition places no mark anywhere between the pe after 18:6 and the pe after 18:31 - so this boundary rests on the register change alone (dialogue and logistics to a march-and-departure notice), disclosed here as an evidenced, not a silent, choice.
strongest_rejected_alternative: The alternative previously tested (splitting v14 from vv15-17) answered the wrong question and left the operative one - whether anything actually begins at 18:18 - unexamined. Tested now: closing at 18:17 and opening a fresh unit at 18:18 was considered and rejected, because 18:18's opening clause repeats material already given at 18:17 rather than introducing anything new; a boundary cannot be anchored on a signal (the priest's challenge) that arrives behind a resumptive clause. The unit is instead closed at 18:20, where the priest's assent and his physical crossing to the Danites is the real terminus, confirmed independently by M8-Judg-145's own already-frozen opening evidence at 18:21. This disclosure follows the standard M8-Judg-140 sets within this same chunk: state the paragraph and parashah evidence in full, including where it might be read to favor an alternative, rather than resting a register-change argument on an undisclosed record - now met here by the paragraph and parashah citations added to this decision's own evidence block.

boundary_rationale: Opens with the group's departure, dependants and goods placed before them (v21), and narrates the pursuit and confrontation. A stated rule now governs the pronoun-fronted circumstantial frame (הֵ֚מָּה / הֵ֥מָּה) across the range: where it introduces no new agent, it is continuative (18:3, opening M8-Judg-139); where it introduces one, it is ordinarily disjunctive and opens a unit (19:22, opening M8-Judg-152). 18:22 (הֵ֥מָּה הִרְחִ֖יקוּ מִבֵּ֣ית מִיכָ֑ה וְהָאֲנָשִׁ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר בַּבָּתִּים֙...נִֽזְעֲק֔וּ) is the one place the principle is not applied to open a unit, and that is now a stated, principled override rather than a silent inconsistency: departure, pursuit, confrontation and retreat here form one continuous escalating encounter carried by vav-consecutive with no reset at any interior seam, and splitting at 18:22 would sever the pursuers' mobilization from the very departure that triggers it. Closes with Micah's retreat home (v26), ending his role in the narrative. v27 shifts to the Danites' continued march with no further reference to Micah.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the departure/pursuit (21-23) from the confrontation-and-retreat (24-26) was considered and rejected, as before. Newly tested: splitting at 18:21/18:22 (departure alone, against pursuit-through-retreat as its own unit) under the new-agent-introduced principle that governs 19:22 elsewhere in this range. Rejected on the stated ground above - the pursuit is the direct and immediate consequence of the departure it follows, and treating 18:22 as an opener here would break a single escalating chain that the campaign keeps whole in comparable cases (e.g., the Gibeah demand-to-assault sequence at 19:22-26 itself, kept whole despite its own internal agent shifts).

literature_type_guess: cultic installation notice and priestly genealogy
boundary_rationale: Opens with the installation of Micah's image among the Danites and the genealogical notice naming the founding priest, printed in the consonantal text as בֶּן מְנַשֶּׁ֜ה, 'son of Manasseh' - no accent mark belongs on the bare בֶּן here (a prior citation error inserted one; corrected below). Rabbinic tradition reads this as the Masorah's suspended-letter device (nun taluy: an extra nun raised above the line, traditionally read as inserted into what would otherwise read Mosheh, 'Moses') - the smoothing move, not the disclosure - but that suspension itself is a scribal/typographic convention this workspace's plain consonantal encoding does not represent in any form: the stored source shows an ordinary בֶּן with no raised letter, no ketiv/qere pair, and none of the marks (U+05C4, U+05C5) this same file uses elsewhere to encode such pairs (compare the bare-form-then-pointed-form sequences at 19:3, 1:27, and 4:11, none of which are present here). The startling detail (a line traced to Moses serving an idol at the book's structural hinge) is preserved instead in the traditional reading that WEB follows ('the son of Moses'), read against the plain consonantal מְנַשֶּׁה the workspace does show. The decision now states the divergence accurately, without asserting a Masoretic device this file cannot itself witness: the plain consonantal text reads 'Manasseh,' the traditional reading follows 'Moses,' and the assigned inputs are silent on which is prior or on how any suspended letter is to be represented. Closes with a second, parallel duration-notice (v31), corroborated by a pe, ending the whole Danite migration complex. Ch19:1 opens the refrain again in its short, unit-opening form.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Unchanged: treating v30 and v31 as two separate decisions was considered and rejected; both are parallel, complementary closing notices about the same installed image with no scene-break or speech-formula between them, reading as one compound closure.
